page: Google Cloud Platform c4d-standard-384 is a high-scale general-purpose instance type built on x86_64 processor architecture. It provides 384 dedicated virtual CPU cores alongside 1488.0 GB of system memory, yielding an allocation of approximately 3.88 GB of RAM per vCPU. This ratio closely mirrors standard enterprise general-purpose configurations while providing an exceptionally large single-system execution domain.

Hardware acceleration is not included, with a GPU count of zero. The instance also features no bundled local storage, requiring persistent disks or network-attached storage volumes for operating system disks and persistent application state. Network provisioning does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses, necessitating configured network gateways or assigned external IP resources for direct public internet routing.

From an infrastructure efficiency perspective, the machine consolidates substantial CPU execution capacity and large memory reserves within a single host environment. This design reduces inter-node networking overhead typical of distributed worker clusters. However, workloads requiring extreme disk throughput must factor in remote storage limits due to the absence of local NVMe storage.

Google Cloud Platform c4d-standard-384 fits large-scale enterprise deployments, multi-threaded batch data processing pipelines, massive continuous integration pools, in-memory analytical workloads, and dense virtualization or container orchestration nodes.
